# Task 3 — Integrate and Construct

## 3.0 Inputs

This document builds directly on Person 1's Task 1/2 outputs and does not
re-clean any data. Reading in the cleaned exports and audit/flag files:

```{r import}
d01 <- read_csv("D01_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                col_types = cols(HouseholdID = col_character(), .default = col_guess()))
d04 <- read_csv("D04_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                col_types = cols(HouseholdID = col_character(), .default = col_guess()))
d05 <- read_csv("D05_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                col_types = cols(HouseholdID = col_character(), .default = col_guess()))
d07 <- read_csv("D07_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                col_types = cols(HouseholdID = col_character(), .default = col_guess()))
d09 <- read_csv("D09_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                col_types = cols(HouseholdID = col_character(), .default = col_guess()))

hh_size_flags <- read_csv("flag_householdsize_mismatches.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
income_flags  <- read_csv("flag_income_mismatches.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("Rows on import — D01:", nrow(d01), "| D04:", nrow(d04), "| D05:", nrow(d05),
    "| D07:", nrow(d07), "| D09:", nrow(d09), "\n")
cat("Flagged HouseholdSize mismatches:", nrow(hh_size_flags),
    "| Flagged income mismatches:", nrow(income_flags), "\n")
```

## 3.1 Target grain and integration strategy

The analytical grain is one row per `HouseholdID`. D04, D05, D07 and D09 are
already at this grain (confirmed in Person 1's §2.7 summary). D01 is
person-level and cannot legitimately be row-joined — joining a person-level
table onto a household-level table on `HouseholdID` alone would silently
fan out the household rows (a one-to-many join), which is not a valid
integration at this grain. The justified alternative is **aggregation**:
D01 is collapsed to one summary row per household first, and only the
aggregated table is joined.

## 3.2 Aggregate D01 to household grain

```{r d01-aggregate}
before_person_rows <- nrow(d01)
before_households  <- n_distinct(d01$HouseholdID)

d01_agg <- d01 %>%
  group_by(HouseholdID) %>%
  summarise(
    HouseholdSize_D01   = n(),
    Age_mean            = mean(Age_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_median          = median(Age_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    N_Dependants        = sum(Age_clean < 15 | Age_clean > 64, na.rm = TRUE),
    Dependency_ratio    = N_Dependants / pmax(HouseholdSize_D01 - N_Dependants, 1),
    N_PopulationGroups  = n_distinct(PopulationGroupCode, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("D01 person-level rows before aggregation:", before_person_rows, "\n")
cat("Distinct HouseholdIDs in D01:", before_households, "\n")
cat("Rows after aggregation (should equal distinct HouseholdIDs above):",
    nrow(d01_agg), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(d01_agg) == before_households)
```

**Verification:** row count after aggregation equals the number of distinct
households in the person-level file, confirming the aggregation is 1:1 at
household grain and safe to join.

## 3.3 Confirm join cardinality before joining

Every household-level file should be 1:1 on `HouseholdID`. This is checked
explicitly before any join is attempted, rather than assumed:

```{r cardinality-check}
check_1to1 <- function(df, name) {
  n_rows <- nrow(df)
  n_ids  <- n_distinct(df$HouseholdID)
  cat(name, "— rows:", n_rows, "| distinct HouseholdID:", n_ids,
      "| 1:1?", n_rows == n_ids, "\n")
}
check_1to1(d01_agg, "D01 (aggregated)")
check_1to1(d04, "D04")
check_1to1(d05, "D05")
check_1to1(d07, "D07")
check_1to1(d09, "D09")
```

`d05` is expected/confirmed here to be a subset of the household population
covered by D04/D07/D09 — this is checked explicitly below via anti-join
rather than assumed, since an unnoticed coverage gap would silently
introduce `NA`s after the join.

## 3.4 Sequential joins with row-count verification

Joins are performed one at a time — not chained in a single pipe — so row
counts can be checked after each step. D04 is used as the base table since
it is confirmed 1:1 and dwelling-level.

D07 and D09 each carry their own copies of `HouseholdSize`,
`HouseholdSize_clean`, `Income_clean` and `TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw`.
Person 1's Task 2 flagged mismatches between these copies
(`flag_householdsize_mismatches.csv`, `flag_income_mismatches.csv`) with no
codebook basis to prefer one over the other row-by-row. Rather than let
`dplyr`'s automatic `_D07`/`_D09` suffixing decide silently based on join
order, every colliding column is renamed explicitly before joining, so it's
unambiguous afterwards which file each figure came from.

```{r join-step1}
n_before <- nrow(d04)
household_data <- d04 %>%
  left_join(d01_agg, by = "HouseholdID")
n_after <- nrow(household_data)
cat("Join 1 (D04 + D01_agg): before =", n_before, "| after =", n_after,
    "| row count preserved?", n_before == n_after, "\n")
```

```{r join-step2}
n_before <- nrow(household_data)
household_data <- household_data %>%
  left_join(d05, by = "HouseholdID", suffix = c("", "_D05"))
n_after <- nrow(household_data)
cat("Join 2 (+ D05): before =", n_before, "| after =", n_after,
    "| row count preserved?", n_before == n_after, "\n")

# Coverage check: how many D04 households have no matching D05 record?
d05_unmatched <- anti_join(d04, d05, by = "HouseholdID")
cat("Households in D04 with no D05 match:", nrow(d05_unmatched), "\n")
```

```{r join-step3}
n_before <- nrow(household_data)
household_data <- household_data %>%
  left_join(
    d07 %>% rename(HouseholdSize_D07 = HouseholdSize,
                    HouseholdSize_clean_D07 = HouseholdSize_clean,
                    Income_clean_D07 = Income_clean,
                    IncomeRaw_D07 = TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw),
    by = "HouseholdID", suffix = c("", "_D07")
  )
n_after <- nrow(household_data)
cat("Join 3 (+ D07): before =", n_before, "| after =", n_after,
    "| row count preserved?", n_before == n_after, "\n")
```

```{r join-step4}
n_before <- nrow(household_data)
household_data <- household_data %>%
  left_join(
    d09 %>% rename(HouseholdSize_D09 = HouseholdSize,
                    Income_clean_D09 = Income_clean,
                    IncomeRaw_D09 = TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw),
    by = "HouseholdID", suffix = c("", "_D09")
  )
n_after <- nrow(household_data)
cat("Join 4 (+ D09): before =", n_before, "| after =", n_after,
    "| row count preserved?", n_before == n_after, "\n")
```

**Final integrated table:**

```{r join-summary}
cat("Final household_data — rows:", nrow(household_data),
    "| distinct HouseholdID:", n_distinct(household_data$HouseholdID), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(household_data) == n_distinct(household_data$HouseholdID))
```

Row count held constant at every step and matches the distinct-household
count throughout, confirming every join was 1:1 (no fan-out) and no
household was duplicated or unintentionally dropped.

## 3.5 Column-level selection: dropping redundant raw income copies

`IncomeRaw_D07` and `IncomeRaw_D09` are the pre-sentinel-cleaned income
figures — the same field `Income_clean_D07`/`Income_clean_D09` were derived
from in Task 2. Keeping both the raw and cleaned versions would mean
carrying two redundant, sentinel-contaminated columns into the final
dataset for no analytical benefit (mirroring Person 1's §1.4 column-level
selection approach: drop columns with no analytical content once a cleaned
equivalent exists).

```{r drop-raw-income}
n_cols_before <- ncol(household_data)
household_data <- household_data %>%
  select(-IncomeRaw_D07, -IncomeRaw_D09)
cat("Columns before:", n_cols_before, "| after dropping raw income duplicates:",
    ncol(household_data), "\n")
```

## 3.6 Derived / engineered features

Each engineered variable below states its source columns, construction, and
the analytical rationale for including it.

```{r derived-features}
household_data <- household_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Services-access index (water + sanitation).
    # Electricity access is not captured in D04 or D05 in this data pack
    # (confirmed against both files' column lists), so it is excluded here
    # rather than substituted with a proxy (e.g. D09's appliance-ownership
    # codes, which measure something different) — a documented limitation
    # rather than a fabricated component.
    Services_access_index = rowSums(cbind(
      PipedWaterCode_clean == 1,    # confirmed via table(d05$PipedWaterCode_clean)
      MainToiletCode %in% c(1, 2)   # confirmed via table(d05$MainToiletCode)
    ), na.rm = TRUE),

    # Income per capita: D07's cleaned income divided by D01-derived
    # household size. D07 is used rather than D09 since Person 1's Task 2
    # flagged the two as mismatched for some households with no codebook
    # basis to prefer one over the other; D07 is chosen here for
    # consistency with the food-security variables this feature is meant
    # to relate to.
    Income_per_capita = Income_clean_D07 / pmax(HouseholdSize_D01, 1),

    # Food insecurity flag: convenience binary from D07's recoded label.
    # A clean 0/1 flag is easier to use in modelling/segmentation than the
    # three-level factor, while the factor itself is retained.
    FoodInsecure_flag = if_else(RanOutOfFood_label == "Yes", 1L, 0L)
  )

summary(household_data$Services_access_index)
summary(household_data$Income_per_capita)
table(household_data$FoodInsecure_flag, useNA = "ifany")
```

## 3.7 Final data dictionary

Retained and engineered variables are tiered qualitatively following
Person 1's §1.3 scheme (High = directly measures resources/access
hypothesised to drive the outcome; Medium = demographic/context variable
that conditions the outcome; Low = administrative/design field, not a
substantive predictor).

```{r data-dictionary}
data_dictionary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Variable,                              ~Source,             ~Type,       ~Tier,     ~Description,

  # --- Key ---
  "HouseholdID",                          "D04/D05/D07/D09",   "character", "Key",     "Household key, join grain",

  # --- D01 (aggregated to household grain) ---
  "HouseholdSize_D01",                    "D01 (aggregated)",  "integer",   "Medium",  "Count of persons per household from D01",
  "Age_mean",                             "D01 (aggregated)",  "double",    "Medium",  "Mean cleaned age of household members",
  "Age_median",                           "D01 (aggregated)",  "double",    "Medium",  "Median cleaned age of household members",
  "N_Dependants",                         "D01 (aggregated)",  "integer",   "Medium",  "Members aged <15 or >64",
  "Dependency_ratio",                     "D01 (engineered)",  "double",    "Medium",  "N_Dependants / working-age members",
  "N_PopulationGroups",                   "D01 (aggregated)",  "integer",   "Medium",  "Distinct PopulationGroupCode values within household",

  # --- D04 ---
  "HeadPopulationGroupCode",              "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Population group of household head",
  "HeadSexCode",                          "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Sex of household head",
  "HeadAge",                              "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Age of household head",
  "MainDwellingCode",                     "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Main dwelling type",
  "WallMaterialCode_clean",               "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Cleaned wall material code",
  "RoofMaterialCode",                     "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Roof material code",
  "FloorMaterialCode",                    "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Floor material code",
  "WallConditionCode",                    "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Wall condition code",
  "RoofConditionCode",                    "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Roof condition code",
  "FloorConditionCode",                   "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Floor condition code",
  "TotalRooms_clean",                     "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Cleaned total rooms in dwelling",
  "TenureCode",                           "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Tenure status code",
  "RentRaw_clean",                        "D04",               "double",    "Medium",  "Cleaned monthly rent",
  "RDPHousingCode",                       "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "RDP housing flag",
  "HousingSubsidyCode",                   "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Housing subsidy flag",
  "HouseholdSize_clean",                  "D04",               "integer",   "Medium",  "D04's cleaned household size (treated as base-table copy)",
  "MetroCode",                            "D04",               "integer",   "Low",     "Metro/non-metro geography code",
  "ProvinceClean",                        "D04",               "character", "Low",     "Canonical province label (base-table copy, from Task 2 §2.0)",

  # --- D05 ---
  "PipedWaterCode_clean",                 "D05",               "integer",   "High",    "Cleaned piped-water access code",
  "WaterSafeCode",                        "D05",               "integer",   "High",    "Perceived water safety code",
  "WaterTreatmentCode",                   "D05",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Water treatment method code",
  "MainToiletCode",                       "D05",               "integer",   "High",    "Main toilet type code",
  "SharedToiletCode",                     "D05",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Shared-toilet flag",
  "ToiletDistanceCode_clean",             "D05",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Cleaned distance-to-toilet code",
  "HandwashingFacilityCode",              "D05",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Handwashing facility availability code",
  "WaterInterruptionFrequencyCode_clean", "D05",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Cleaned water-interruption frequency code",

  # --- D07 ---
  "AdultHungerCode",                      "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Adult hunger indicator code",
  "ChildHungerCode",                      "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Child hunger indicator code",
  "WorriedFoodWouldRunOutCode",           "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Food-insecurity worry indicator code",
  "UnableToEatHealthyFoodCode",           "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Diet-quality food-insecurity code",
  "FewFoodsDays_clean",                   "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Cleaned days eating few food types",
  "SkippedMealDays_clean",                "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Cleaned days meals were skipped",
  "AteLessDays_clean",                    "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Cleaned days ate less than needed",
  "RanOutDays_clean",                     "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Cleaned days food ran out",
  "RanOutOfFoodCode",                     "D07",               "integer",   "High",    "Raw ran-out-of-food code, Stats-SA convention 1/2/9",
  "RanOutOfFood_label",                   "D07",               "character", "High",    "Recoded label (Yes/No/Don't know-refused); provisional pending GHS codebook",
  "HouseholdSize_D07",                    "D07",               "integer",   "Low",     "D07's own HouseholdSize copy, kept for transparency (see §3.4 note)",
  "HouseholdSize_clean_D07",              "D07",               "integer",   "Low",     "D07's own cleaned HouseholdSize copy, kept for transparency",

  # --- D09 ---
  "MainIncomeSourceCode_clean",           "D09",               "integer",   "High",    "Cleaned main income source code",
  "SocialGrantRecipients",                "D09",               "integer",   "High",    "Number of social grant recipients in household",
  "TotalGrantRecipients",                 "D09",               "integer",   "High",    "Total grant recipients in household",
  "SalaryEarnersInHousehold",             "D09",               "integer",   "High",    "Number of salary earners in household",
  "VehicleAssetCode",                     "D09",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Vehicle ownership indicator code",
  "TotalVehicles_clean",                  "D09",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Cleaned total vehicle count",
  "FridgeAssetCode",                      "D09",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Fridge ownership indicator code",
  "FreezerAssetCode",                     "D09",               "integer",   "Medium",  "Freezer ownership indicator code",
  "HouseholdSize_D09",                    "D09",               "integer",   "Low",     "D09's own HouseholdSize copy, kept for transparency",
  "Income_clean_D07",                     "D07",               "double",    "High",    "D07's cleaned income; used as the authoritative income figure (see §3.4)",
  "Income_clean_D09",                     "D09",               "double",    "Low",     "D09's cleaned income, kept for transparency but not used in Income_per_capita",

  # --- Engineered (§3.6) ---
  "Services_access_index",                "D05 (engineered)",  "integer",   "High",    "Count of adequate water+sanitation indicators (0-2); electricity excluded, not captured in this data pack",
  "Income_per_capita",                    "D07 (engineered)",  "double",    "High",    "Income_clean_D07 / HouseholdSize_D01",
  "FoodInsecure_flag",                    "D07 (engineered)",  "integer",   "High",    "1 = RanOutOfFood_label == 'Yes', else 0"
)
kable(data_dictionary, caption = "Data dictionary — retained and engineered variables")
```

*(Note: the D04/D05/D07/D09 rows above document the columns retained after
Task 2's cleaning and Task 3's joins; if any additional low-relevance
administrative columns — e.g. `SurveyYear`, `GeoTypeCode`,
`HouseholdWeight` — are also being retained downstream for correct
survey-weighted estimation per Person 1's §1.3 note, add them here as
"Low" tier rather than omitting them silently.)*
